entry.content: A Professional Insight in which the authors examine Russia's war in Ukraine and destabilisation of Europe to show how hybrid warfare is financed through illicit networks. They argue that the FATF and states need new typologies, metrics and controls to disrupt the funding.

entry.title: Cutting Through the Myths of Blockchain Analysis
entry.content: In this Feature, an investigator challenges the idea that blockchain analysis is too complex. Using his own practice, he argues that simple, systematic wallet labelling can expose large-scale illicit crypto activity, and calls for analytics firms and regulators to refocus on this work rather than hype-driven tools.
entry.dc:creator: RUSI Publications

entry.title: Sanctions and the Militarisation of Ukraine's Children
entry.content: Russia’s mass abduction and militarisation of Ukrainian children is a grave abuse. This Feature assesses how far current sanctions address the problem and argues for broader measures that target the camps, officials, businesses and banks enabling it.
entry.dc:creator: RUSI Publications

entry.title: Revision to FATF Recommendation 8: Impacts on Sub-Saharan Africa
entry.content: FATF Recommendation 8 was intended to protect legitimate charities, but in practice many sub-Saharan African governments have used it to justify blanket, costly regulation of non-profit organisations. This Research Article examines how over implementation harms civic space and financial access.
entry.dc:creator: RUSI Publications

entry.title: Is the Financial Action Task Force Fit for the Future?
entry.content: In this Research Article, the author argues that the FATF’s current enforcement model, especially greylisting, is ill suited to lower-income countries. She calls for more representative governance and a shift from sanctions towards cooperative, interaction based compliance.
entry.dc:creator: RUSI Publications

entry.title: The FATF Needs to Tackle How War is Financed
entry.content: Conflict financing sits at the heart of many grey- and blacklisted jurisdictions, yet the FATF has never treated it as a distinct, cross cutting risk. In this Professional Insight, the author calls for a dedicated report on how wars are funded, to guide more nuanced, risk-based responses and strengthen the organisation’s credibility with conflict affected states.
entry.dc:creator: RUSI Publications

entry.title: The Dual Burden of FATF Compliance for Developing Countries
entry.content: In this Research Article, the author shows how developing countries carry a dual burden under the FATF system: costly efforts to build effective AML/CFT regimes; and the added economic fallout of greylisting when they fall short. She argues that mutual evaluations and listing should be context sensitive to avoid undermining reform in lower-capacity states.

entry.title: Proliferation Financing Risk Assessments
entry.content: A Professional Insight which argues that FATF proliferation financing risk assessments are being applied too narrowly, overly focusing on North Korea and Iran.
